title: How B-Tree Indexes Speed Up SQL Queries 1000x
subtitle: Stop table scans: how databases locate rows in milliseconds
summary: Without an index, the database executes a Full Table Scan O(N), checking millions of rows. A B-Tree index acts like a book index, finding targets in logarithmic O(log N) disk reads.
key_points: Structure: Self-balancing multi-way search tree where leaf nodes form a doubly linked list.
Clustered vs Non-Clustered: Clustered determines physical row storage order (Primary Key). Non-clustered stores indexed columns with pointers to the data rows.
Composite Index: An index on (user_id, created_at) must follow the Leftmost Prefix Rule to be utilized.
Trade-off: Speeds up SELECT queries, but adds write overhead on INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE because the index tree must rebalance.

complexity.lookup_time: O(log N) - typically 3 to 4 disk I/O operations
complexity.storage: Consumes 10% - 30% additional disk space per table

interview_tip: Be prepared to explain when NOT to use an index: small tables (<1000 rows), frequently written/updated columns with rare reads, or columns with low cardinality (like boolean flags).
